title: Microsoft Edge: choose a profile at startup with a profile picker
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says the Windows Group Policy and registry controls also apply on macOS, where Microsoft documents preference keys instead. It also understates the documented reach of the picker and profile-creation policies and describes targeted browser policies as tenant-wide controls.

claims.claim: The Group Policy path is Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Profile settings > Profile picker availability.

GP name: Profile picker availability
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Profile settings
claims.fix: Use 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Profile settings > Profile picker availability' for computer-scoped domain Group Policy. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge for the entry route; User Configuration is the alternative user scope.

claims.claim: The cited Learn policy pages state no licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge for Business licensing requirements profile picker price charge. Opened ProfilePickerAvailability, BrowserGuestModeEnabled and BrowserAddProfileEnabled in full; none states a licence requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this startup profile-picker feature yet.
claims.quote: This policy controls whether users can open the profile picker in Microsoft Edge. The profile picker lets users choose a profile to open and manage their profiles.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'The roadmap describes the profile choices and Show on startup setting; Microsoft Learn documents the profile picker and its startup policy behaviour through ProfilePickerAvailability.' Keep the narrower absence concerning the Show on startup setting.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the Show on startup user setting or a policy setting that configures that preference.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge "Show on startup" profile picker policy default guest. Read ProfilePickerAvailability, privacy On startup, and Initial Preferences excerpt; none names that preference. Picker availability policy is documented separately.

claims.claim: The picker policy is not confirmed by name for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: the browser skips the profile picker at startup and follows its normal browser startup behavior.
claims.fix: Replace 'Not confirmed by name for the roadmap feature' and the corresponding prose caveat with 'Controls availability of the profile picker, including at startup.' Remove the question asking whether this policy governs the picker; retain the question about configuring Show on startup.

claims.claim: All three policies are Group Policy or registry settings on Windows and macOS.
claims.quote: This article describes how to configure Microsoft Edge on macOS using a property list (.plist) file.
claims.fix: Replace with 'The table gives Windows Group Policy and registry settings. On macOS, Microsoft documents the preference keys ProfilePickerAvailability, BrowserGuestModeEnabled and BrowserAddProfileEnabled in a com.microsoft.Edge.plist file.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge-on-mac and qualify each existing row's surfaces as Windows.

claims.claim: None of these Edge browser policies is a Microsoft 365 admin centre setting.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Edge management service is a platform in the Microsoft 365 admin center that enables admins to easily configure Microsoft Edge browser settings for their organization.
claims.fix: Remove 'and none of them is a Microsoft 365 admin centre setting'. The Edge management service documents browser policy configuration in that centre; the briefing need not add a new control row or assert that each named policy appears in its current setting catalogue.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; controls[1].scope; controls[2].scope; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The listed Group Policy and registry controls have tenant scope.
claims.quote: You can scope policy settings to either the Computer Configuration or User Configuration by selecting the appropriate node as described below.
claims.fix: Set all three controls[].scope values to 'other' and add 'Applies to targeted Windows computers or users through Group Policy or registry configuration; not automatically tenant-wide' to their notes. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge.
